name: Yellow Apatite
physical: Traditionally linked to vitality and zest
Associated with a warm, lively feeling
Kept nearby by many for energy and motivation
summary: Yellow apatite is a bright lemon-gold phosphate, famous from Durango in Mexico, linked in crystal lore to confidence, joy and personal willpower.
intro: Yellow apatite glows like a lemon drop. The crystals are hexagonal prisms with a bright, glassy luster, ranging from pale straw to a deep, buttery gold, and they often have a greenish tinge in some light. The best-known deposits are in Durango, Mexico, where beautifully terminated crystals have been collected for generations and are sometimes called asparagus stone because of the greenish-yellow shade. Gem-quality pieces are faceted into soft, cheerful gems for collectors, but because the stone is relatively soft, it is more commonly sold as a specimen. It is a happy, sunny stone, and that is exactly how people tend to describe the feeling it gives.
history: Apatite got its name from the Greek apatao, to deceive, because it so often resembled other gems like peridot, beryl and citrine. It was formally named by Abraham Werner in 1786. The yellow variety from Cerro de Mercado in Durango, Mexico, is a classic find, collected from iron deposits where the crystals sit in a rusty red matrix, making a striking display. Yellow apatite appears in other places as well, including Madagascar and Canada. Because apatite is also the main mineral in bone and teeth, it holds a particular significance in biology. Modern crystal practitioners treat the yellow type as a stone of the sun.
meaning: Yellow apatite is associated with confidence, self-esteem and personal will. Its golden-yellow color links it to the solar plexus, so practitioners use it to boost motivation, to stand up for oneself and to recover from low moods. It is also considered a stone of joy, helpful when you feel flat or unmotivated. Many people place it on a desk when launching a project, because its sunny color is said to fuel willpower. Some also use it for creative flow and as a gentle companion for mental clarity. Traditionally it is associated with warmth, a lively mood and a feeling of vitality, particularly during dark winter months.
howToUse: Keep a piece of yellow apatite on your desk or in your pocket to touch whenever you need a confidence boost. Hold a crystal while writing an affirmation in the morning, and place it in a sunlit corner of your room (but out of direct sun) to brighten the atmosphere. A pendant or earrings with yellow apatite keep the sunny energy close. In a grid with citrine and clear quartz, it forms a sparkling motivation layout. It is a good gift for a friend starting a new job or trying something brave.
care: Yellow apatite is soft, scratches easily and can fade in strong sunlight, so protect it from heat and harsh light. A brief rinse in lukewarm water is safe, but avoid soaking, ultrasonic cleaners and acidic cleaners. Cleanse with moonlight, sound, smoke or selenite. Store it separately in soft cloth, away from harder stones like quartz, and remove jewelry before activities where it might be knocked.
identify: Natural yellow apatite shows a bright, glassy yellow to yellow-green color and hexagonal crystal shape, often in a reddish iron-rich matrix from Durango. Citrine is harder and more orange, while yellow fluorite is softer and has cubic cleavage. Yellow glass or dyed quartz can imitate the shade but lacks the crystal habit. Apatite scratches easily with a knife, which is a helpful test for sellers but should be done only on inconspicuous spots.

faq.q: What is yellow apatite good for?
faq.a: People use yellow apatite for confidence, joy and willpower. Its sunny yellow is tied to the solar plexus, so it is kept on desks, in pockets or worn as jewelry when someone needs a boost.

faq.q: Where does yellow apatite come from?
faq.a: The most famous source is Cerro de Mercado in Durango, Mexico, where bright yellow crystals sit in iron-rich rock. It is also found in Madagascar, Brazil, Canada and Spain.

faq.q: Can yellow apatite go in sunlight?
faq.a: It is best to avoid long exposure. Yellow apatite can fade in strong sun and heat, so cleanse it with moonlight, sound or smoke and display it where it receives soft light rather than direct rays.
